'''Rachel Margolis''' (28 October 1921 &ndash; 6 July 2015) was a Lithuanian [[List of Holocaust survivors|Holocaust survivor]], [[Partisan (military)|partisan]], [[biologist]] and Holocaust historian.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2010/jan/08/holocaust-baltic-lithuania-latvia?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT3487 |title= Halting Holocaust obfuscation |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=8 January 2010 |accessdate=17 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Rašel Margolis|url=http://www.lzb.lt/category/uzuojautos/|publisher=lzb|accessdate=18 July 2015|language=Lithuanian}}</ref>

==Background==
Margolis was born in [[Vilnius]], Lithuania in 1921.<ref name="Keene"/> Her parents were Jewish. In 1941, when the [[Nazis]] occupied Lithuania, Margolis was sent to live with a Christian family. She instead decided to voluntarily enter the Jewish [[Vilna Ghetto]] in September 1942. She entered the resistance movement there and became active in the underground. She joined the [[Fareynikte Partizaner Organizatsye]], formed that same year by poet [[Abba Kovner]]. Margolis wrote<blockquote>"Everyone was anxious to fight... Our mission was to acquire weapons, complete militarily preparations, all with the aim of provoking an uprising in the ghetto. If we perished it would be with honour, having proved to humanity that we are not sheep going meekly to the slaughter."<ref name="Courage">{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/women-of-courage-rachel-margolis-2236081.html |title=Women of courage: Rachel Margolis |date= 9 March 2011 |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |accessdate=24 January 2013}}</ref></blockquote>In June 1943, [[Heinrich Himmler]] commanded the extermination of the ghetto. 4000 Jewish residents were sent to death camps and killed; 4000 more were sent to labour camps. Margolis and her future husband were one of the few hundreds that survived the ghetto, by escaping to the surrounding forests. They contracted [[typhus]] but lived to continue their work with the resistance movement, joining a new unit and blowing up German infrastructure.<ref Name="Courage"/> Margolis was the only member of her family to survive the Holocaust .<ref Name="Courage"/><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZNI79jJnsOoC |author=Kazimierz Sakowicz |title=''Ponary Diary 1941-1943: A Bystander's Account of Mass Murder'' |date=January 2005 |isbn=0300108532 |editor=Yitzhak Arad}} Published in Polish in 1999 by Towarzystwo Milosnikow Wilna i Ziemi Wilenskiej and Rachel Margolis. Translation copyright 2005 [[Yad Vashem]]. p. vii</ref> Her mother and brother perished in the [[Ponary massacre]].<ref name="Sakowicz2005" />

==Post war==
After the war, Margolis gained a Ph.D. in biology and was a teacher until the end of the 1980s. She helped establish Lithuania's only Holocaust museum, the Green House in Vilnius.<ref name="Keene">{{Cite web |url=http://sites.keene.edu/cohencenter/rachel-margolis-lithuanian-partisan-and-survivor/ |title=Profile at the Cohen Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies |publisher=[[Keene State College]] |access-date=2012-09-28 |archive-date=2018-02-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180221183506/http://sites.keene.edu/cohencenter/rachel-margolis-lithuanian-partisan-and-survivor/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Her work in the resistance has been honoured by US congress and the British House of Lords.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/opinion/2009/0530/1224247744866.html |date=5 May 2009 |title='Genocide industry' has hidden agenda |newspaper=Irish Times |access-date=28 September 2012 |archive-date=12 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110812151242/http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/opinion/2009/0530/1224247744866.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref Name="Campaign"/>

Margolis's 2010 memoir ''A Partisan of Vilna'' recounts the author's escape from the Vilna Ghetto with the FPO (United Partisan Organization) resistance movement and the time spent in the forests of Lithuania with the partisans, active on sabotaging missions.<ref Name="Courage"/><ref>{{Cite book |last=Margolis |first= Rachel |title=''A Partisan of Vilna'' |location=Brighton, MA |publisher=Academic Studies Press |year=2010}}</ref>

Margolis found and published the long-lost diary of [[Kazimierz Sakowicz]], a Polish Christian journalist who witnessed the [[Ponary massacre]] outside Vilnius, where tens of thousands of Jews were murdered.<ref name="guardian">{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2010/jan/08/holocaust-baltic-lithuania-latvia?INTCMP=ILCNETTXT3487 |last= Katz |first=Dovid |title=Halting Holocaust obfuscation |newspaper=The Guardian |date= 8 January 2010 |accessdate= 17 September 2012}}</ref> Margolis reconstructed Sakowicz's diary from fragments of paper found in lemonade bottles, text written on a 1941 calendar and other papers held in archives that were not accessible under Soviet rule.<ref name="Sakowicz2005">{{cite book |author=Kazimierz Sakowicz |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZNI79jJnsOoC |title=Ponary Diary, 1941-1943: A Bystander's Account of a Mass Murder |publisher=Yale University Press |year=2005 |isbn=978-0-300-10853-8 |pages=vii–xii}}</ref>

Beginning in 2008, the Lithuanian prosecutor general wanted to question Margolis as part of the investigation of the [[Koniuchy massacre]] when Soviet and Jewish partisans killed at least 38 civilians.<ref Name="Campaign">{{Cite news |title=''Wiesenthal Center Protests Lithuanian Judicial Campaign to Discredit Jewish Heroes of Anti-Nazi Resistance'' |publisher=[[US Fed News Service]] |date=28 May 2008}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Don't let Holocaust be rewritten out of history |work=[[Washington Jewish Week]] |date=31 December 2009}}</ref> Lithuanian newspapers referred to her as a terrorist and a murderer.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.jpost.com/LandedPages/PrintArticle.aspx?id=102678 |title=I have fought once, I can fight again |date= 28 September 2012 |newspaper=[[Jerusalem Post]]}}</ref>

Margolis also lived in [[Rehovot]], Israel.<ref name="guardian" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pcHHNBuuE9s |title=Interview with Rachel Margolis on YouTube |website=[[YouTube]] |accessdate=17 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.jpost.com/Magazine/Features/Article.aspx?id=183781 |newspaper=Jerusalem Post |title=''Digging up the future'' |date=8 June 2010}}</ref>
